Subject: TTFT targets + streaming connectivity / fallback plan (post-demo recap)

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciate the clear product goals and latency sensitivity notes. Quick recap from our side + proposed next steps so we can align on a pilot that validates your Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and streaming UX constraints.

Call summary (high level)
- BlueHarbor goal: conversational assistant in mobile app with perceived immediate response and progressive rendering. Target median TTFT ~120-200ms on LTE; 95th <= 400ms.
- Preferred streaming mode: SSE for ease of reconnection and native browser support in your webview, but you asked about WebSocket fallback for poor network cases.
- Chunk cadence: you'd like small early chunks for quick UX (first chunk <= 50 tokens) then larger steady chunks.
- Concurrency: typical user concurrency per device is 1-2 concurrent streams; expected peak throughput ~400-600 rps during peak events.

Proposed pilot plan (short):
1) Benchmark baseline: our hosted endpoint + small sample model with your typical payloads to record TTFT distribution (median / p50, p90, p95).
2) Streaming test matrix: SSE primary (heartbeat + auto-reconnect), WebSocket as explicit fallback path, and HTTP long-poll as last resort for very flaky networks. We'll test chunk sizes: 32 tokens (fast-first), 64 tokens, 128 tokens and cadence intervals: immediate-first + 150ms pacing vs 250ms pacing.
3) Load test: simulate 600 rps with concurrency per connection = 1 and 2; measure per-token CPU, tail latencies, and KV cache effectiveness.
4) Integration checks: mobile SDK integration review (webview SSE compatibility), and fallback logic for reconnects and duplicate chunk handling.

Action items / owners
- Ben (me): schedule pilot env provision and share probe plan + Drive link (today).
- Marissa: propose initial model/quantization profile for pilot (tomorrow).
- Jonas: validate load test configuration and resource estimate (Wednesday).
- Alicia / Samir: provide sample requests (representative prompts, typical token lengths) and a short network trace (attached) if possible.

Attachments: TTFT pilot probe plan (spreadsheet) — contains test payloads and measurement fields.

If that aligns, I'll provision a dedicated pilot token and share test endpoints by EOD.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben — this looks great and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and constraints from our side:

- Environment: our mobile app uses an embedded webview on iOS and Android. SSE is supported but iOS webview has been flaky under cellular + backgrounding; we expect some connections to drop frequently.
- Network profile: median RTT on LTE in our target region is ~60ms, but we see 200-400ms spikes in fringe cases.
- Blackbox constraint: our back end adds ~30-50ms enroute for pre-processing. So we need Redwood to be <= 150ms median TTFT at the edge to meet perceived target.
- Chunk tolerance: our renderer expects chunk boundaries with explicit token offsets or JSON framing (we prefer framed JSON chunks).

We'll attach a short (30s) network trace and a small set of sample prompts — Samir attached the prompts. On the fallback question: we prefer WebSocket for low-latency bidirectional requirements but only as a fallback if SSE reconnects exceed 3 attempts. For very bad networks, we'll fall back to 1s long-polling but expect degraded UX.

Next steps: please include a recommended heartbeat interval and a suggested duplicate-detection idempotency approach for reconnects. Also note that our security team needs to confirm that streaming tokens expire or can be revoked on-demand.

Thanks,
Alicia

Alicia / Ben — quick technical notes from infra/runtime perspective: we can hit ~120–180ms median TTFT for small models on our hosted endpoints with the following optimizations enabled: warm cold-start pools, KV prefix caching, and low-latency kernel selection. P95 will depend heavily on network and pre-processing though.

Heartbeat / reconnect / idempotency suggestions (initial):
- Heartbeat: 15s SSE comment frames to detect half-open connections.
- Reconnect policy: client attempts 0,1,2 backoff (500ms, 1s, 2s) and on 3rd failure switch to WebSocket fallback; if WS fails after 2 attempts, switch to long-poll at 1s.
- Idempotency: provide per-stream session id (uuid v4) and per-chunk sequence numbers; on reconnect, client includes last-seen seq to let server resume or retransmit missing chunks. We can also include a small resume token in the stream metadata.

Chunk cadence recommendations to validate in trial:
- First chunk: <= 50 tokens within 80–120ms from request acceptance.
- Follow-ups: pacing of 150–250ms with 64–128 token windows depending on model compute.

Load testing notes (Jonas to detail): simulate 600 rps with real token distributions, measure p50/p95/p99 TTFT and tokens/sec. We'll also validate the overhead of our SSE connection handling (per-connection file descriptors and sockets under high concurrency).

I'll sketch these into the pilot probe sheet and attach a first-pass model profile.

—Marissa

Quick runbook for the load test / metrics we'll collect:

Test topology
- Client pool simulating 1k unique devices (to account for bursts) at 600 rps sustained for 10 minutes, ramp 30s.
- Concurrency per connection: test scenarios with 1 and 2 concurrent streams.
- Models: small-v1 (quantized 4-bit) and medium-v1 (FP16) to see compute differences.

Metrics
- TTFT: p50 / p90 / p95 / p99 (ms) measured at both client and server side (we'll correlate with probe traces).
- Chunk arrival latency: time difference between token generation and client receipt per chunk.
- CPU / GPU utilization and ephemeral memory per-worker.
- Connection churn: SSE reconnects per minute and WS fallback counts.
- Error surface: partial responses, duplicate-chunk events, resume failures.

Acceptance criteria (initial)
- Median TTFT <= 180ms (client-observed) for small-v1 under nominal network profile.
- P95 <= 400ms for small-v1; if not met, we'll iterate on chunk cadence and model profile.

I'll provision a sandbox endpoint (read-only token) and post the load test script to the Drive later today. Ben — can you confirm the sample prompts Alicia mentioned so I can embed them in the scenario?

Thanks,
